## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
Sign pictures are not described: only meanings stated in the manual's text are taught, and the sign images and their colors-by-picture are left to the media layer.
The color list conflicts on school signs: one passage gives yellow as the background for warning and school signs, while the same page and the next name fluorescent yellow-green as the school zone color; only fluorescent yellow-green is taught for school zones (verify TN-SIGN-D-SCHOOL) [A01].
The manual says a regulatory sign is always a rectangle, yet the octagonal stop sign and triangular yield sign also regulate traffic; it is taught only as rectangles carrying laws and regulations, not as an exclusive rule (verify TN-SIGN-D-SHAPE) [A01].
The manual speaks of nine basic background colors but describes fluorescent pink as an additional incident color [A02]; both are taught by their stated use without a color count.
The extracted chapter heading repeats the vehicle chapter title, and several pages extracted with split words and picture labels; only body text whose meaning was unambiguous was used [A06].

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 49 lists yellow as the background for warning signs and school signs, while physical pages 49 and 50 name fluorescent yellow-green as the school zone color; confirm the current Tennessee school sign color.

Physical page 49 says a regulatory sign is always a rectangle, while physical page 50 describes the octagonal stop sign and triangular yield sign that also regulate traffic; confirm how the test treats regulatory sign shapes.
